name: UK inflation & rates
summary: Bank of England raised Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023; CPI 3.5% in September
state: UK CPI inflation was 3.5% in the 12 months to September, inside the 2.5–4.0% Watch band (ONS). The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, reversing its easing cycle (Sovereign Magazine). October CPI is due on 18 Nov.
for_you: Higher rates feed through to variable mortgages and new loans; savings rates also tend to rise.
rubric_hit: CPI 3.5% in 2.5–4.0% band and BoE reversing course = Watch
basis_detail: ONS CPI and Bank of England decisions
basis_by: ONS CPI and Bank of England decisions

sources.title: Sovereign Magazine — Bank of England rate rise, November 2026

why: UK inflation and the Bank Rate set mortgage, savings and business borrowing costs for the whole country.
drivers: Energy prices, wages, services inflation, sterling, global rates.

rubric.alert: CPI > 4.0%, or an emergency BoE move.
rubric.watch: CPI 2.5–4.0%, or the BoE reversing course.
rubric.normal: CPI ≤ 2.5% and Bank of England moving gradually or on hold.
